XXXVII  nota  (29):  Wycliffe  here  opens  as  a  corollary  (to 
former  statements)  what  was  doubtless  one  of  the  principal 
objects  he  had  in  writing  the  book  (De  Dom.  Civ.),  namely 
the  assertion  of  the  rights  of  the  civil  state  over  the  pro- 
perty of  the  Church,  in  the  case  of  the  latter  misusing  her 
trust.  He  recurs  to  it  frequently  in  the  sequel.  The  passio- 
nate energy  of  the present  chapter shows  elo- 
quently the  vital  importance  which  JW  attached  to  the 
doctrine  now  announced  and  his  almost  defiant  consciousness 
of  the  opposition  to  which  its  avowal  would  necessarily  ex-
